סברו שמצוה להתענות בר"ה וממילא לא עשו ע"ת כיון דלא שייך בו כדי שיברור מנה יפה לשבת ומנה יפה ליו"ט אך עזרא אמר להם לכו אכלו משמנים והודיע להם שמצוה לאכול בר"ה א"כ שייך בו כדי שיברור מנה יפה לשבת ומנה יפה לי"ט וממילא בעי ע"ת לכך שלחו מנות לאין נכון לו וא"ש ודו"ק הארכתי בזה והבאתי ראיות לכאן ולכאן ישמע חכם ויוסיף לקח וע"ע בדין אם מצוה להתענות בר"ה בחיבורי על תורה משנת תרט"ו בפרשת נצבים ע"ש בעזה"י ודוק:
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_.en: Seif 1 — they eat and drink and rejoice and do not fast on Rosh Hashanah, etc. It appears to me: see in Beit Yosef and Taz what they brought — two views on this. And it appears to me there is proof from gemara that there is a dispute of tannaim — from what is taught in Taanit chapter 3: that city fasts and sounds teruah and all surroundings fast and do not sound; R' Akiva says they sound and do not fast. Tosefot brought in the name of Yerushalmi explaining their dispute: Tanna Kamma compares to Yom Kippur where they fast and do not sound; R' Akiva compares to Rosh Hashanah where they sound and do not fast — end. If so Yerushalmi is explicit on Rosh Hashanah there is no mitzva to fast, for this is R' Akiva's reason deriving from Rosh Hashanah where they sound and do not fast. But in truth one must understand why Tanna Kamma compares to Yom Kippur and why the other compares to Rosh Hashanah — in what reasoning do they argue? Therefore it appears in truth all agree it was more fitting to compare to Rosh Hashanah than Yom Kippur; only Tanna Kamma holds on Rosh Hashanah there is mitzva to fast — if so on Rosh Hashanah they fast and sound teruah — and teruah without fasting we do not find; but conversely fasting without teruah we find on Yom Kippur — therefore he holds fast and do not sound. But R' Akiva holds there is no mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah — if so you find teruah without fasting — therefore he holds sound and do not fast. And one could also say: for Tanna Kamma it is a kal va-chomer that there is mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah — for per Tanna Kamma teruah is inferior to fasting — he holds fast and do not sound — if so kal va-chomer for Rosh Hashanah: where they do not sound they fast — where they sound, namely Rosh Hashanah — all the more they should fast; therefore kal va-chomer that on Rosh Hashanah one must fast. Conversely for R' Akiva one cannot learn kal va-chomer — since for him fasting is inferior to teruah — he holds sound and do not fast — if so learn kal va-chomer: where they do not fast they sound — where they fast, namely Yom Kippur — all the more they should sound — we would sound on Yom Kippur! This is not so — on Yom Kippur since it is explicit in Torah that only on Yom Kippur of Jubilee they blow, it is clear on ordinary Yom Kippur they do not blow; but for Rabbanan there is no explicit verse that one does not fast on Rosh Hashanah — therefore properly learn kal va-chomer: where they do not sound they fast — all the more where they sound one should fast; therefore for Tanna Kamma there is obligation to fast on Rosh Hashanah; but for R' Akiva there is no obligation to fast on Rosh Hashanah; and since we hold like Tanna Kamma there — it is more reasonable like the view that there is mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah as I wrote — requires study. Some bring proof from the verse of Ezra and from Elisha that there is no obligation to fast on Rosh Hashanah. In my opinion there is no proof at all, as known — fasting is in place of sacrifice; therefore certainly in Temple times when we had the Temple and actual sacrifices there was no obligation to fast — by Torah law no obligation and no prohibition to fast; therefore conversely by reasoning it is fitting to eat and rejoice as Ezra said. But for us without Temple and without sacrifices — one could say there is mitzva to fast so we have fasting in place of sacrifice — and all the above proofs are rejected. With this it appears to explain Kohelet "rejoice in youth," etc. — "and know that for all these Hashem will bring you to judgment" — this refers to Rosh Hashanah — only through joy and confidence do they become similar to Him may He be blessed and fit to come with Him in judgment. We explain what midrash says: when Hashem ascends and sits on the throne of judgment — in judgment He ascends — sometimes when Israel are not worthy Hashem as it were lowers Himself and judges Israel below as said "I dwell with the crushed"; if they are worthy Hashem elevates them above as the other tanna taught "I am with the crushed." With this one understands gemara Rosh Hashanah 26a properly in what it argues: one says on Rosh Hashanah as much as a person's mind is settled is better; on Yom Kippur as much as his mind is depressed is better; and the other says on Rosh Hashanah as much as mind is settled is better, and on fast days as much as mind is depressed is better. At first glance one does not understand in what reasoning they argue. It appears thus: Rashi explained "as much as mind is depressed is better" — as written "and My eyes and heart shall be there all the days"; and on "as much as mind is settled" Rashi explained — as written "let us lift our hearts to our palms." In Yevamot it states, brought in Tur Even HaEzer: one says eyes should be downward — "and My eyes and heart there all the days"; another says the pray-er must have heart upward — "lift our hearts to our palms," etc. — explicit: verse "eyes and heart" — looking downward; verse "lift our hearts" — looking upward. With this we understand the matter — as we wrote, without confidence we would not be fit for Him to come with us in judgment; if He comes it is only kindness as Baal HaAkedah said — then He lowers Himself; but if they have confidence in Him they become like Him and are fit to come in judgment with them — then He elevates them. In every matter action and proof are needed — thought alone does not help — one must bring everything from potential to actual; likewise trials of Abraham — though all was revealed before Him, Hashem wanted to bring the matter from potential to actual; if so here too for confidence thought in heart is not enough — one must bring confidence from potential to actual. Therefore if they eat and drink on Rosh Hashanah — this shows great confidence in their hearts — as Ezra said "eat fat foods," etc., "for the joy of Hashem is your strength" as explained there; but if they fast on Rosh Hashanah there is no joy and no hint of confidence. But on Yom Kippur of Jubilee — although they fast, since then fields return and slaves go free — there is no greater monetary loss than this; if they lacked confidence in Him they would fear monetary loss — perforce they are confident in Him — also a hint of confidence; with this one explains the whole sugya: he who says on Rosh Hashanah as much as mind is depressed is better — meaning they fast on Rosh Hashanah and there is no remembrance of confidence — consequently not fit to come in judgment except by kindness as Baal HaAkedah — then Hashem lowers Himself — he holds like "I dwell with the crushed" — therefore one could say as much as mind is depressed is better — as "eyes and heart there all the days" — Hashem as it were lowers Himself below. But on Yom Kippur of Jubilee where there is great confidence in this itself — sending all free — therefore fit to come with them in judgment and then He elevates them — he holds like "I am with the crushed" — therefore on Yom Kippur as much as mind is settled is better — as "lift our hearts to our palms" — hinting eyes upward as Yevamot. The other who says mitzva to eat on Rosh Hashanah and rejoice — if so since there is actual deed showing confidence — fit to come with them in judgment — he holds like "I am with the crushed" — therefore as much as mind is settled is better. But on other fasts where there is no sending slaves and fields and no joy — no hint of confidence — judgment is certainly only kindness as Akedah said — therefore as much as mind is depressed is better — understand, I shortened. I wonder on those who hold mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah from mishnah Chullin chapter 5 83 and brought in Avodah Zarah 5b: in these chapters one must inform "I sold my cow today," "I sold my maidservant today," and lists also Rosh Hashanah — thus proven on Rosh Hashanah mitzva to increase eating like other festivals — even more than Shabbat which is not listed there — proven on Rosh Hashanah mitzva to increase eating more than Shabbat. But per Magen Avraham here that at night certainly forbidden to fast — one could say both exist: at night mitzva to increase meal like every festival; by day mitzva to fast — understand. I have further proof for those who forbid fasting on Rosh Hashanah from Tosafot chapter 3 of Shevuot that one may fast on Rosh Hashanah — from what they wrote 20b s.v. when he did not vow they challenged Rashi who erased the text concluding: since it is rabbinic, etc. — if it were d'oraisa the vow would not take effect for vows do not take effect on fulfillment of a mitzva — see there. Still Rashi's words are correct — for we say in Rosh Hashanah when there is no persecution they want to fast they may, when persecution they may not — if so when there is persecution at least when he vowed generally to fast on the day Gedalyah was killed it includes forever; once he vowed it takes effect when there is no persecution when they do not want to fast — if so since it applies when no persecution it applies also when there is persecution and it is properly a vowed matter — why does gemara need to say since rabbinic, etc. — requires study at first glance. Perforce their intent is: Gedalyah was killed on Rosh Hashanah only his fast was postponed to a weekday — if so if he vows "like the day Gedalyah was killed" his intent is not on the fast day but on Rosh Hashanah itself when he was killed; and what seemed that it is not a vowed matter is from mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah — nevertheless certainly no mitzva d'oraisa only rabbinic; nevertheless "includes" does not apply here since forever there is mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah — therefore properly they wrote if d'oraisa the vow would not take effect — requires study well. Later authorities bring proof forbidden to fast on Rosh Hashanah from Nechemiah "eat delicacies and drink sweets and send portions to one who has nothing prepared." In my opinion this does not apply — on the contrary proof the opposite — why did he first mention their eating then say send portions to one unprepared — should have said send portions first then eat delicacies? It appears from this there will be proof mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah. Sifrei Musar wrote: if one eats and in the middle of eating stops — that is better than fasting. Therefore in Yoreh Deah siman 119 it states: if suspected of selling forbidden items — if he sent a gift to his house it is permitted to eat — presumption from what he eats he sends to him — as custom of sender of food to friend sends what he eats. Therefore Ezra told them in this manner they may eat — if first they eat then take from their food and send portions — this is considered as if they fasted. Thus Ezra told them: in this manner eat delicacies and drink sweets — meaning "and send portions" from what you took to eat send to one unprepared — this is like fasting — implies conversely forbidden — thus proven conversely mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah. However it appears to me clear proof forbidden to fast on Rosh Hashanah — if one could fast on Rosh Hashanah, I am very puzzled from gemara and Choshen Mishpat siman 199: four chapters Chazal established their words on Torah law — tears, constellations, and one is Rosh Hashanah — if one could hold mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah why did Chazal enact here tears constellations? One cannot say for the nights — for on Shabbat they did not enact Ben even though mitzva of oneg — since joy is not written they did not enact; but on festival since "you shall rejoice on your festival" and joy is only with meat they enacted thus — if one could say Rosh Hashanah is not included in "you shall rejoice on your festival" why did they enact more than Shabbat? Perforce "you shall rejoice" includes also Rosh Hashanah — if so the day too is included like every festival — this is clear proof in my opinion — requires study. Further proof forbidden to fast from chapter 2 of Beitzah where they argue reason for eruv tavshilin — one says so he will set aside a nice portion for Shabbat and a nice portion for festival and they learned from "remember the Shabbat day" — remember it after it comes to be forgotten. Difficult — main eruv tavshilin we learn from Ezra's verse send portions to one unprepared — if we say mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah — behold on Rosh Hashanah there is no obligation of joy at all — how say he will set aside nice portion for Shabbat and festival — on Rosh Hashanah he lacks obligation of joy — why should it be less than every Shabbat for which they made no enactment? Perforce obligated to eat and drink on Rosh Hashanah — therefore eruv tavshilin applies; if Rosh Hashanah eating is reshut — why need Rosh Hashanah for Shabbat? Therefore requires eruv tavshilin; if eating reshut — no superiority over weekday — why need Rosh Hashanah for Shabbat? And do not say this is only for the view whose reason is to set aside — for the other view who says so they will say from festival to weekday — all the more one could say mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah — this is not so — for then why did it not say the other version that for the view to set aside there is mitzva to eat on Rosh Hashanah and for the view to say — mitzva to fast? Perforce they do not argue on this; and since for the view to set aside perforce proven on Rosh Hashanah mitzva to eat — likewise for the view to say. Possible to explain continuation of Ezra's verse: go eat fat foods and drink sweets and send portions — Chazal said for one who did not place eruv tavshilin — what connection? Intent: they thought mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah — therefore did not make eruv tavshilin since it does not apply to set aside nice portion for Shabbat and festival; but Ezra told them go eat fat foods and informed them mitzva to eat on Rosh Hashanah — if so eruv tavshilin applies to set aside nice portion for Shabbat and festival — therefore send portions to one unprepared — understand and requires study. I expanded here and brought proofs both ways — let the wise hear and add learning — and see in my judgment whether mitzva to fast on Rosh Hashanah in my Torah works year 556 in parashat Nitzavim — see there with Hashem's help — examine.

levushei-serad/3:_.he: סק"ג קידושא רבא וכו'. ר"ל קידוש דשחרית הנקרא קידושא רבא אבל בריש סימן רפ"ט במ"א שם מבואר דקידוש זה אפי' בשבת הוא דרבנן ומכ"ש ביו"ט דנתבאר בריש סי' רע"א במ"א סק"א דאפי' קידוש הלילה ביום טוב הוא דרבנן משא"כ בשבת דקידוש הלילה הוא דאוריית':
levushei-serad/3:_.en: So, and so on. Hashem’s Word is called the Holy Spirit, but He is a sign of Hashem’s presence in the Holy Spirit, and He is a blessing for Hashem’s mercy on the earth, and he is blessed with Hashem’s Word on a good day

machatzit-hashekel/3:ב.he: דאנן קי"ל שהוא דרבנן. שבסי' רפ"ט כתב דאפי' בשבת שקידוש לילה דאורייתא מכל מקום קידוש יום דרבנן. ובסי' רע"א כתב דבי"ט אפילו קידוש של לילה דרבנן. וגם בשבת אי כבר התפלל יצא מן התורה במה שהזכירו בתפלה ע"ש:
machatzit-hashekel/3:ב.en: (ב) Dr. Dain, who is a dragon. In S. R. R.R., Dufa wrote on Saturday that a night was filled with creeds from everywhere to the day of Darbin. And in S. Bada, he wrote, "Damn't even a sway of the night of Darin." And on the Shabbat, the Torah has been prayed in what is mentioned in the darkness:

magen-avraham/3:א.he: המתענה . כתוב בתשו' מהר"ם ססי' נ"ד מהר"ם התענ' וקידש בביתו קידוש' רבא ואמר הטעם לפי שהוא דאורייתא עכ"ל ועסי' רפ"ט דאנן קי"ל שהוא דרבנן ועמ"ש רסי' רע"א ומ"מ נ"ל דבלילה של ר"ה אסור להתענות כמו בשאר י"ט כמ"ש סי' תקכ"ט ע"ש דבחלום לא הראוהו אלא ביום ולא בלילה:
magen-avraham/3:א.en: (א) answered. It is written in the Hashem’s house, and he said, “He is the same as the Hashem’s Prayer, and that he is the Hashem’s Prayer, and that He is the Hashem’s Prayer, and that He is the Hashem’s Prayer, and that He is not the Hashem’s Prayer.”
